english_draft:
This is a historical reconstruction. It was not written before the target-quarter earnings. It uses only Amazon's first-quarter 2026 earnings release, published on April 29, 2026. The target event is the second-quarter 2026 earnings release.

1. Conclusion. Amazon enters the second quarter with strong momentum. First-quarter net sales grew 17 percent. AWS growth accelerated to 28 percent. The main risk is free cash flow pressure from artificial-intelligence capital spending. The second-quarter report will show whether AWS growth and cash generation remain strong.

2. Baseline from the first quarter. Net sales were $181.5 billion. This was an increase of 17 percent from $155.7 billion in the first quarter of 2025. Excluding foreign exchange, net sales increased 15 percent. North America sales were $104.1 billion, up 12 percent. International sales were $39.8 billion, up 19 percent. Excluding foreign exchange, International sales increased 11 percent. AWS sales were $37.6 billion, up 28 percent. Operating income was $23.9 billion, compared with $18.4 billion. Net income was $30.3 billion, or $2.78 per diluted share. This includes pre-tax gains of $16.8 billion from Anthropic investments. Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow was $148.5 billion, up 30 percent. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was $1.2 billion, compared with $25.9 billion. The decrease was driven by a $59.3 billion increase in property and equipment purchases, mainly for artificial intelligence.

3. Key questions for the second quarter. Question one: Can AWS maintain the 28-percent growth rate or grow faster? Question two: Will capital spending continue to pressure free cash flow? Question three: Will Prime Day in June and advertising growth support retail results?

4. Scenarios. Positive scenario: AI demand continues to grow. New Trainium or Bedrock agreements strengthen the AWS outlook. Prime Day drives retail and advertising growth. Negative scenario: The Anthropic gain does not repeat. Free cash flow worsens. AWS growth decelerates. International growth remains weak without foreign-exchange support.

5. Verification points. Check total net sales and segment sales. Check segment operating income. Check AWS growth. Check free cash flow and capital spending. Check for new non-operating gains. Check management commentary on artificial-intelligence investment and the third-quarter outlook. No quantitative guidance for the second quarter appears in the available source.
